AUTHOR: Shevchenko
TITLE: Fish Detection from Low Visibility Underwater Videos
DATA: Own/partner fish-pass videos from Kymijoen vesi ja ympäristö ry: Dataset 1 (2013, 4 videos), Dataset 2 (2016, 6 videos)
V_EV: Sec. IV-A: 'the average distance between the camera and the fish is 55 cm'; Sec. I: 'videos from muddy water with various types of illumination and visibility'
D2: no train/test split; unsupervised background subtraction evaluated on all videos
D_EV: Sec. IV-C: 'Adaptive GMM and KDE methods were taken from the OpenCV library [19] and were used with default parameters' (no training split described)
R_EV: Sec. IV-A: 'Dataset 2 was gathered by the same organization in 2016' — untrained methods evaluated on both datasets; parameter R set individually per dataset
E_EV: Table I: 'Results of the experiments with threshold for IoU of 0.5. Three values in each cell refer to P, R and F1'
ARCH: Background subtraction (Adaptive GMM, KDE, ViBe) + morphological post-processing + optical flow + size/direction heuristics
METR: Frame-level precision, recall, F1 at IoU 0.5; F1 vs IoU threshold curve
NOTE: Classical unsupervised background-subtraction detector (no supervised learning); included as ML/CV detection on field fish-pass video but borderline on AI criterion (a). No training split exists, so D coded NR. 2013 vs 2016 datasets from same fish pass; no model trained on one and tested on other, so R1=N. V6=P: per-video results discussed qualitatively in terms of darkness/visibility (Dataset 2 darker; 72-93% when fish distinguishable vs 50-87% low visibility). V3 coded Y from qualitative illumination description of own data.
